title: Meeting Boyd and his first Raeburn writing
summary: Jack Siegel's song led to arranging for Boyd and joining on piano; he recalls early pop charts and 'Is You Is'.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: How did you run into Boyd at the beginning?

I was introduced to him by Jerry, the manager. I explained to you how my friend Jack Siegel--he wasn't my friend then, I didn't know him either, I was introduced to Jack as the writer of the song called 'Who Started Love' and he needed to get his song into Boyd's library because Boyd had a wire out of the hotel and Jack wanted to get his song on the air. The way to do it was to get somebody to write an arrangement to give to Boyd, and so, I don't recall exactly, but I think probably Jack paid for it, rather than Boyd, and that's how Boyd and I met, as the
arranger of Jack's song. Boyd was impressed with the chart and asked me if I would like to write for the band, and that's how it began. After a little while, I joined the band on piano.
Do you remember what you wrote in those days, any of the material?
It would be difficult to recall.
Nothing that has survived into this library?
There was a thing--I wrote a thing for Trummy Young to sing on our theater tour, which was "Is You Is Or Is You Ain't My Baby"; I recall that one.
I imagine there were a whole bunch of nondescript pop tunes, publisher's material that came through in the early days that I wrote, but I don't really remember those things.
That was essentially a sort of a gray or non-important part of the career. You were just writing pop tunes and
The piano playing must have been notable now and then. You were still you.

In those days I had a kind of self confidence that I don't think was really too genuine. Deep inside of me I didn't enjoy my piano playing and so I couldn't take compliments as being genuine and that's the way it's been most of the time.
The band didn't record anything during that period, did it?
There were some dates but I don't remember them recording anything of mine.
